evidence.estrutura: Heller's later liberal-democratic philosophy emphasized constitutional institutions, pluralism and active citizenship rather than territorial centralization; no strong federal-versus-unitary doctrine is central.
evidence.representacao: Her mature political thought explicitly defended liberal democracy, deliberation, multiparty representation and active citizenship against elective autocracy.
evidence.poder: Her life under Nazism and Stalinism and later criticism of Orbán-era authoritarianism strongly support limits on arbitrary state power, civil liberties and constitutional checks.
evidence.imigracao: Her work on minorities, universalism and pluralism supports inclusion and equal citizenship, though not a specific open-borders program.
evidence.diplomacia: Her anti-totalitarian and cosmopolitan liberal commitments support international cooperation and dialogue rather than nationalist militarism.
evidence.intervencao: She was anti-totalitarian but not a doctrinaire pacifist; the evidence supports skepticism toward coercive domination while leaving room for rights-based collective action.
evidence.economia: Heller moved from Marxism toward a center-left liberal-democratic position, supporting social equality and welfare concerns without retaining a command-economy model.
evidence.controle: Her later thought rejected Stalinist planning and bureaucratic control while accepting democratic social institutions; this supports moderate regulation rather than centralized planning.
evidence.comercio: No detailed tariff doctrine is central to her work; her later liberal-democratic outlook is compatible with international openness but not laissez-faire absolutism.
evidence.religiao: Her political theory is secular and grounded in ethics, dignity and constitutional pluralism rather than religious authority.
evidence.moral: Her work on ethics, autonomy, minority rights and later New Left themes supports socially progressive and pluralist positions.
evidence.tecnologia: Her work on biopolitics considered moral and legal limits on genetic and biological technologies, supporting a cautious, human-centered rather than accelerationist technology stance.
